message.content:
Here are **five of the most pollinator‑friendly flowering plants native to South America**—chosen for their abundant nectar/pollen, long blooming periods, and attractiveness to bees, butterflies, hummingbirds, and other pollinating insects:

| # | Scientific name | Common names (English / Spanish) | Why it’s great for pollinators |
|---|-----------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1 | *Heliconia rostrata* | Heliconia, “Lobster Claw” | Produces large, brightly coloured bracts that attract hummingbirds; also offers pollen for bees and butterflies. Bloom lasts several weeks. |
| 2 | *Canna indica* | Canna lily, “Siam Tulip” | Dense clusters of nectar‑rich flowers that feed bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Blooms year‑round in tropical climates. |
| 3 | *Passiflora edulis* | Passion fruit, “Maracujá” | Flowers open at night and day, attracting both moths and bees. Provides ample pollen and nectar; also yields edible fruit. |
| 4 | *Mimosa pudica* | Sensitive plant, “Touch-me-not” | While known for its touch‑responsive leaves, it produces small but plentiful flowers that supply pollen to solitary bees and wasps. |
| 5 | *Erythrina crista‑galli* | Coral tree, “Palo de gallina” | Large, bright red inflorescences that are highly attractive to hummingbirds and some bee species. Blooms throughout much of the year. |

These species are well‑adapted to South American ecosystems, produce generous rewards for pollinators, and can often thrive in gardens or restoration projects aimed at supporting local insect and bird populations.
